battle.name: 一二八事變
battle.brief: 一二八事變發生於1932年1月28日至3月3日的上海，日軍以八九式戰車等現代化武器突破華界，與國民革命軍激烈交戰，並在公共租界周邊展開激烈巷戰，測試並展示日本帝國的軍事實力與對華政策的强硬立場。

kit.name: 八九式戰車
kit.history: 作為日本帝國陸軍首款大規模生產的中型戰車，於1932年的一二八事變中投入上海戰場，提供機動火力支援。

countries: 這裏所說的「一二八事變」採上海事件的通常含義，即1931年11月28日至1932年1月31日的上海戰事；名稱所指的1932年1月28日，是日軍再次大規模進攻的日期。中華民國一方的核心兵力是國民革命軍第十九路軍，中央軍第五軍等部隊在戰役後段接應；日本帝國一方以日本陸軍上海派遣軍作戰，先後投入第三、第六、第十一師團等，並由海軍陸戰隊、長江與黃浦江的艦隊、海軍航空隊協同。英國、美國與法國的租界界線是外部限制因素，這三國不是主要交戰方，但其管轄範圍影響停火線的劃定。1932年1月31日停火，2月18日另簽上海停戰協定。
countriesEn: This refers to the Shanghai Incident in the usual sense, covering the fighting in Shanghai from November 28, 1931, to January 31, 1932. January 28, 1932, is the date associated with the renewed Japanese offensive and with the incident's name. The principal Chinese force was the Nineteenth Route Army of the National Revolutionary Army, while Central Army units including the Fifth Army arrived later to support the fighting. Japan fought through the Imperial Japanese Army's Shanghai Expeditionary Army, committing the 3rd, 6th, and 11th Divisions at different stages, supported by the naval landing force, warships in the Yangtze and Huangpu River, and naval aviation. The concession boundaries of Britain, the United States, and France were external constraints, and those three countries were not principal belligerents, although their jurisdiction affected where the ceasefire line was drawn. Fighting stopped on January 31, and the Shanghai Truce Agreement was signed on February 18.
people: 蔣介石在南京掌握中央政府的調兵與政治決定，張治中則以第十九路軍總指揮身份主持上海防務，決定各師的佈防、撤退和停火線上的指揮。前線師級指揮包括第八十七師師長戴安瀾；日方由上海派遣軍司令白川義禁統籌全局，第十一師團長吉澤小三郎等在前線實施攻擊，海軍指揮官負責艦砲掩護、登陸與交通線。戰役前段，張治中把防守重點放在虹橋、閘北、吳淞、寶山和江灣等北部要點，第十九路軍各師依托固定陣地互相支援；十二月底以後，南京調來的第五軍等中央軍部隊進入戰線。實際指揮受到道路、通信距離和彈藥運輸的限制，中央軍與第十九路軍的交接並非同時完成。
peopleEn: Chiang Kai-shek in Nanjing controlled Central Government reinforcement and political decisions. Zhang Zhijiang, as commander of the Nineteenth Route Army, directed Shanghai's defense, including deployment, withdrawal, and command along the ceasefire line. Dai Anlan, commander of the 87th Division, was an important divisional commander at the front. On the Japanese side, General Shirakawa Yoshinori, commander of the Shanghai Expeditionary Army, coordinated the operation, while Lieutenant General Yoshizawa Kozaburo, commander of the 11th Division, and other commanders directed attacks in the field. Naval commanders coordinated naval gunfire, landings, and movement along the supply routes. In the first phase, Zhang concentrated the defense at northern points including Hongqiao, Zhabei, Wusong, Baoshan, and Jiangwan, and the divisions of the Nineteenth Route Army supported one another from fixed positions. After late December, Central Army units including the Fifth Army entered the line. In practice, road conditions, communications distances, and ammunition transport limited command; the handover between the Central Army and the Nineteenth Route Army was not completed at one moment.
kits: 1931年的中、日軍械並不相同。第十九路軍步兵主要使用八八式步槍，中文常稱七九式，射擊七點九二毫米彈藥；部分連隊配ZB-26輕機槍，固定火力使用Maxim式水冷重機槍，並有八二毫米迫擊砲與七五毫米野戰砲、山砲。日軍步兵主要以一九〇五年制式三八式步槍作戰，使用六點五毫米彈藥，連級火力採十一年式輕機槍，火砲包括七五毫米野戰砲、山砲，海軍另有艦砲；八九式中戰車在一九三一年已列裝，是當時可用的日軍裝甲裝備，但上海前線只由少量裝甲部隊使用，不能把它寫成全線裝甲攻擊。兩軍把步槍彈、機槍彈和砲彈分庫轉運，中方七點九二毫米與日方六點五毫米彈藥不能互換，七五公釐砲彈還需由馬匹、車輛或小型運輸車送到射擊陣地，機槍彈則隨分隊補充；日軍可利用長江口、黃浦江的艦船和碼頭補給，中方則以南京後方軍械庫、滬寧鐵路及上海轉運站接上火線。
kitsEn: Chinese and Japanese equipment in 1931 was not the same. Nineteenth Route infantry mainly used the Type 88 Gewehr, commonly called the Type 79 rifle, firing 7.92-mm ammunition. Some companies had ZB-26 light machine guns, while fixed firepower included Maxim-type water-cooled heavy machine guns, 82-mm mortars, and 75-mm field and mountain guns. Japanese infantry mainly used the Type 38 rifle, adopted in 1905, with 6.5-mm ammunition. The Type 11 light machine gun provided company-level support, while Japanese artillery included 75-mm field and mountain guns, with naval guns adding further firepower. The Type 89 I-Go medium tank had entered service by 1931, but only small armored units used it on the Shanghai front; it should not be described as an all-arms armored assault. Both sides separated rifle, machine-gun, and artillery ammunition in their supply systems. Chinese 7.92-mm and Japanese 6.5-mm ammunition could not be used interchangeably. Seventy-five-millimeter shells had to be carried by horses, vehicles, or small transport carts to firing positions, while machine-gun ammunition traveled with the units. Japan could supply its forces through ships and wharves at the Yangtze mouth and Huangpu River, while China connected the front through the Nanjing arsenal, the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway, and rear transfer stations.
tactics: 十一月二十八日的第一階段衝突集中在上海北部。日軍先把海軍陸戰隊和步兵分隊推到虹口、閘北及吳淞外圍，以火砲和機槍火力封鎖路口，再以小股步兵沿北四川路、虹橋至寶山的道路試探突破；中方沒有沿整條市界同時反擊，而是把第十九路軍固定在虹橋、閘北、吳淞、寶山、江灣一線，用土木工事、機槍巢、迫擊砲和七五公釐火砲組成相互支援的據點。側翼受擊時，前線先以電話或傳令兵求援，預備隊由縱深道路趕到，再做短距離反擊。日軍在後續階段利用登陸部隊從側後切入，以艦砲壓制中國砲兵，並用航空隊偵察、轟炸軍事陣地和補給道路；中國守軍則利用夜間地形重新佈防，切斷日軍孤立前哨。戰線拉長後，局部反擊常因彈藥和通信不及而未能擴成一次總反攻。
tacticsEn: The first phase of the fighting on November 28 was concentrated in northern Shanghai. Japan first moved the naval landing force and infantry toward Hongkou, Zhabei, and the outskirts of Wusong, using artillery and machine-gun fire to seal intersections, then tested breakthroughs with small infantry columns along North Sichuan Road and the roads from Hongqiao toward Baoshan. China did not counterattack simultaneously along the entire city boundary; it held the Nineteenth Route Army on the Hongqiao–Zhabei–Wusong–Baoshan–Jiangwan line, using field fortifications, machine-gun nests, mortars, and 75-mm guns as mutually supporting strongpoints. When a flank was attacked, the front line called for help by telephone or runner, and reserves came forward along roads behind the line to make short counterattacks. In later phases, Japan used landing forces to cut in from the flank and rear, naval guns to suppress Chinese artillery, and aircraft to reconnoiter and strike military positions and supply roads. Chinese troops used the terrain to reestablish positions at night and cut off isolated Japanese outposts. As the front lengthened, local counterattacks often could not become a general counteroffensive because ammunition and communications support arrived too slowly.
data: 日期、路線和編制可以整理成一條較清楚的時間線。1931年11月28日，上海北部日軍與中國守軍交火；十二月下旬起，日本增兵和海軍協同使前線壓力增加；1932年1月上旬，新的師團到達後，日軍在寶山、吳淞、江灣、虹橋等方向反覆試圖切斷中方南北通道，1月28日前後再次發動大規模攻勢；1月31日停火，2月18日簽署協定。中方作戰序列以第十九路軍為主，中央軍第五軍等後續到達；日方作戰序列以上海派遣軍為統帥，師團與海軍陸戰隊、艦隊及航空隊分開指揮但協同作戰。前線北接長江口吳淞，東西連接閘北、虹橋與江灣，後方物資先由南京沿滬寧鐵路到上海，再以汽車、船舶或畜力車分送各陣地。各方兵力、彈藥消耗和傷亡數字並沒有同一套可靠總表，因此可列日期與編制，不能把估算的傷亡數字當成精確事實。
dataEn: Dates, routes, and formations can be arranged as a clear timeline. On November 28, 1931, Japanese and Chinese troops clashed in northern Shanghai. During late December, Japanese reinforcements and naval cooperation increased pressure on the front. In early January 1932, additional divisions arrived, and Japanese attacks repeatedly sought to cut China's north–south routes at Baoshan, Wusong, Jiangwan, and Hongqiao; around January 28, Japan launched another major offensive. Fighting stopped on January 31, and the agreement was signed on February 18. The Chinese order of battle centered on the Nineteenth Route Army, with Central Army units such as the Fifth Army arriving later. Japan's Shanghai Expeditionary Army formed the higher command, while divisions, the naval landing force, warships, and aviation retained separate chains of command but operated together. The front ran from Wusong at the Yangtze mouth through Zhabei, Hongqiao, and Jiangwan. Supplies moved first from Nanjing to Shanghai by the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway, then by motor vehicle, ship, or animal-drawn cart to the positions. No single reliable total exists for the troops, ammunition consumption, or casualties on all sides, so dates and formations can be stated, but estimated casualty figures should not be presented as exact facts.
cause: 直接原因並非一個毫無爭議的單一事件，而是1931年日本在東北得手後，上海軍政權力出現連續摩擦。日本陸軍要求中國軍隊撤退，並為上海衝突道歉；中國政府拒絕後，日本以海軍陸戰隊和增兵施加壓力，談判逐漸被火砲取代。十一月下旬的觸發經過，中日兩方留下的說法並不相同：日方說中國軍警攻擊日本哨位，中方說日本部隊先以武裝封鎖和挑釁方式迫使守軍後退。兩種說法都涉及軍隊的權限和直接接觸，不能簡化為孤立的口頭爭執。更深的背景，是日本試圖把東北形成的壓力延伸到上海，而國民政府仍要保有上海防務與國家主權；第十九路軍奉命駐紮，遂成為日軍選擇的主要對手。
causeEn: The immediate cause was not a single event that could be treated as uncontested. After Japan's military success in Northeast China in 1931, friction over military and political authority continued in Shanghai. The Japanese Army demanded that Chinese troops withdraw and that China apologize for the clash. After the Chinese government refused, Japan applied pressure with the naval landing force and reinforcements, and negotiation was gradually replaced by artillery fire. Accounts of the late-November trigger differ: Japan said Chinese security forces attacked a Japanese post, while China said Japanese troops first used armed obstruction and provocation to force the defenders back. Both accounts concern military authority and direct contact, so the incident cannot be reduced to an isolated verbal dispute. The deeper background was Japan's attempt to extend the pressure created by its position in Northeast China to Shanghai, while the Nationalist government still intended to retain control of Shanghai's defense and national sovereignty. The Nineteenth Route Army was stationed there and consequently became the principal opponent selected by Japan.
impact: 戰役的第一個直接影響，是上海北部的控制與補給線都發生了變化。日軍把新增師團、艦砲、航空隊和登陸部隊結合起來，使中國守軍在吳淞、寶山、江灣、虹橋一線的若干陣地失守或必須後撤；第十九路軍原有的固定防線被切斷成數段，中央軍第五軍等增援只能在有限時間內重新佈置。與此同時，停戰線成為新的軍事邊界，雙方在線外仍保留兵員和火力，外國租界的存在使上海形成分隔的武裝區。這場戰鬥也讓南京更清楚看到中央軍調度、地方軍作戰、砲兵火力與海空協同之間的差距；第十九路軍因長期抵抗而取得政治聲望，但聲望不等於補給線恢復，也不等於陣地全部守住。各方對傷亡總數的記載互相矛盾，本文只確認作戰時間、部隊番號和武器類型，不列無法核實的精確傷亡。
impactEn: The first direct effect was that control and supply lines in northern Shanghai changed. Japan combined newly arriving divisions, naval gunfire, aviation, and landing troops, forcing Chinese defenders to lose or abandon some positions along Wusong, Baoshan, Jiangwan, and Hongqiao, and breaking the original fixed defense of the Nineteenth Route Army into separate sections. Central Army reinforcements such as the Fifth Army could redeploy only within a limited time. At the same time, the ceasefire line became a new military boundary, both sides still kept troops and firepower outside it, and the existence of the foreign concessions left Shanghai divided into armed zones. The fighting also showed Nanjing the gap between Central Army mobilization, local army operations, artillery fire, and naval-air cooperation. The Nineteenth Route Army gained political prestige through its prolonged resistance, but prestige did not restore supply lines or hold every position. Records of total casualties conflict; this account confirms only the dates, unit designations, and weapon types and does not give an unverifiable precise casualty figure.
result: 到了1932年1月下旬，日軍把後續到達的師團投入寶山、吳淞、江灣與閘北方向，並以艦砲和航空隊支援連續攻擊；中方第五軍等增援雖曾填補部分防線缺口，但前線經反覆消耗，通信、彈藥補給和側翼反擊未能同時維持，最終只能依停火命令退出部分陣地。1月31日雙方停止大規模交火，實際控制線被固定在上海北部若干要點之間，並非日軍完全占領上海，也不是中國軍隊收復全部失地。2月18日簽訂的《上海停戰協定》把停火、駐軍區和撤軍安排寫入文本，日軍依協定分批撤出或調整占領區，中國軍隊也調整了部署。這就是事件的軍事結局：一場以停火和分區控制收束、而非以全面殲滅或全面收復收束的戰役；其傷亡總數仍不宜用單一精確數字概括。
resultEn: By late January 1932, Japan committed the divisions that had arrived later to the Baoshan, Wusong, Jiangwan, and Zhabei directions and supported repeated attacks with naval guns and aircraft. Chinese reinforcements such as the Fifth Army did fill some gaps, but after repeated operations the front could not maintain communications, ammunition supply, and flank counterattacks at the same time; Chinese troops eventually withdrew from some positions under the ceasefire order. On January 31, both sides stopped large-scale fighting, and the actual line of control was fixed among several points in northern Shanghai. Japan did not occupy all of Shanghai, nor did the Chinese army recover every lost position. The Shanghai Truce Agreement signed on February 18 set out ceasefires, garrison zones, and withdrawal arrangements. Japan withdrew from or adjusted occupied areas in stages under the agreement, and the Chinese army also revised its deployments. Thus the military ending was a ceasefire and partition of control, not annihilation on one side or full reconquest by the other; the total casualties still cannot responsibly be reduced to one precise number.
